title.narrative: ICRC - DR Congo 2024-2025 - International Committee of the Red Cross through Danish Red Cross

description.narrative:
This allocation through Danish Red Cross to International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) contributes to ICRC’s activities responding to the humanitarian needs in DR Congo.
In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as elsewhere in the world, the ICRC works according to its principles of neutrality, impartiality, and independence. Its role is to protect the lives and dignity of victims of armed violence.
ICRCs teams work as closely as possible with the communities concerned to monitor whether they are being respected and protected by the parties to the conflict and can meet their basic needs. ICRC reunites separated family members and visit people who have been arrested and detained to ensure that they are treated with dignity.
ICRC helps the wounded, the sick and victims of sexual violence to gain access to health care. The organisation helps the most vulnerable people maintain or regain a stable livelihood, and improves access to water and hygiene. Furthermore, ICRC promotes knowledge of and respect for international humanitarian law and universal humanitarian principles among civil society, authorities and weapon bearers.
